header: THE PAX DIRECTORY SEARCH: reading the question and matching it against the rows (step 63a). I keep it PURE: no database, no model, no clock, so every rule here is tested offline. PAX = the land-line phone that works only inside DSP work areas (5 digits). The numbers are kept by the Telecom department in the table `public.pax_directory` (sql/12). What a person can ask (all answered from the table, never from a model):
- a NAME to a number: "pax number of fire service", "fire service pax", "pax c&it", "pax of civil a zone", a misspelling ("pax fire servise")
- a NUMBER to a name: "who has 42046", "42046" (only if it really is in the directory), "pax 42046", "pax 420" (all numbers that start so)
- a LIST or a COUNT: "pax", "pax directory", "list all pax numbers", "how many pax numbers", "pax numbers outside plant", "township pax numbers"
- a FAULT: "pax not working", "pax complaint" (the Telecom complaint numbers)
- an AREA: "in plant" / "township" / "outside plant" narrows any of the above

ALIASES (my rule, 31 Oct 2026): "pax number", "phone number" and "contact number" are ONE keyword. The SUBJECT decides what the number is: a department, a place or any other non-human entity gives its PAX number (this file and answer.ts); a person who is an executive (ticket 4xxxxx) gives his or her CUG mobile number (people.ts, route.ts). The plan only reads the words; the route decides. WHEN THE ROUTE TAKES A QUESTION (a wrong confident answer is worse than no answer, so I am careful): STRONG cue = the word "pax": always ours (a found answer, or an honest "not found"). WEAK cue = phone, telephone, contact, extension, extn, intercom, landline: ours ONLY when the subject is found (a directory entry, or an executive); never when the question is about a doctor, the hospital OPD, a mobile number, a fault or a circular, and never when nothing is found (the other routes then answer as before). NO cue = ONE bare 5-digit number (with only words like "who has") is ours ONLY when that number is in the directory; otherwise the question goes on untouched. I never take a number of six or more digits (a ticket, a mobile) or a word about circulars (notice, policy, tariff ...).

members.name: label
doc: Keeps the name exactly as printed in Telecom's list ("Civil (A - Zone)").

members.name: deptName
doc: I split the label into the department part and the location part (the location is empty when the list does not say). I use these for matching only.

members.name: id
doc: The row's id in the table: it is known when the row was read from the database, and the panel needs it to modify or delete the row.

members.name: curated
doc: True for a line made or changed in the panel: its department and location are exactly what the HOD typed (deptName, location), and I never guess them from the printed name.

symbols.name: PaxPlan
symbols.sig: | { kind: "number"; claim: "always" | "ifFound"; numbers: string[]; area: PaxArea | null; count: boolean } | { kind: "name"; claim: "always" | "ifFound"; tokens: string[]; optional: string[]; area: PaxArea | null; count: boolean; fault: boolean } | { kind: "person"; claim: "ifFound"; ticket: string } | { kind: "list"; claim: "always"; area: PaxArea | null; count: boolean }

symbols.name: normalizePax
doc: I lower-case the text, remove accents, read "&" as "and" and turn every other mark into a space: "C & IT (Console)" -> "c and it console".

symbols.name: QUERY_STOP
doc: Filler words of a question, never part of a name. "a" is in this list too: it is also the zone in "Civil (A - Zone)", so I can never require it.

symbols.name: ROW_STOP
doc: Filler of the ROWS: I drop only the joining words.

symbols.name: editDistance
symbols.sig: export function editDistance(a: string, b: string, max = 2): number
doc: Edit distance with swapped neighbours counted as one edit (optimal string alignment); I stop early above `max`.

symbols.name: allowedEdits
doc: How many spelling slips a word of this length may have: I allow none in short words, and a 4-letter word must keep its first letter (gate is never date).

symbols.name: matchToken
symbols.sig: export function matchToken(q: string, tokens: Set<string>): TokenHit | null
doc: Does one word of the question match one of the row's words? I accept an exact match, a prefix ("hosp" for "hospital", "services" for "service"), or a spelling slip.

symbols.name: DOCUMENT_WORDS
doc: I treat a question about a document, not the directory, as not mine ("pax billing notice", "tariff for ...").

symbols.name: PEOPLE_WORDS
doc: For a question about a person, a doctor or the hospital OPD I leave the answer to the other routes, unless the word "pax" itself is there.

symbols.name: OUT_AREA
symbols.sig: const OUT_AREA = /\b(?:township|outside (?:the)?plant|out side plant|out of (?:the)?plant|outside area|outer plant)\b/

symbols.name: FAULT
symbols.sig: const FAULT = /\b(?:complain|complaint|complaints|complained|fault|faults|faulty|not working|out of order|no tone|no dial tone|dead|re …
doc: I read a fault as a question about the complaint desk ("PAX Complain" in the list).

symbols.name: TICKET_WORDS
doc: These words only introduce a ticket number.

symbols.name: closeUpNumbers
doc: I close up the digit groups of the text when they make a 5-digit number ("42 046", "42-046" read as 42046); I do this only when "pax" itself is in the question.

symbols.name: planPaxQuery
symbols.sig: export function planPaxQuery(typed: string): PaxPlan | null

members.name: corrections
doc: Words of the question read through a spelling slip: [asked, read as]. I always say these to the person, never silently.

members.name: closest
doc: Filled when nothing matched: the names that share some of the words.

members.name: closestRows
doc: When nothing matched: the rows of the entries that share the MOST words (every one of them, up to 40: "all the SH"). I show them WITH their numbers as related entries, never as the exact answer.

members.name: closestShared
doc: The words of the question that those entries share.

symbols.sig: const AREA_ORDER: Record<PaxArea, number> = { plant: 0, outside: 1, unclassified: 2 }

doc: I count every row once: the same name and number twice is one row.
